stem: Points $A({=Ax}, {=Ay})$ and $B({=Bx}, {=By})$ are the end points of a line segment. Plot the mid-point $M$ of $AB$.
solution: Add the two x-coordinates and divide by 2: $M_x = \dfrac{A_x + B_x}{2}$.
Add the two y-coordinates and divide by 2: $M_y = \dfrac{A_y + B_y}{2}$.
notes: Rows are chosen (unlike the book's own ex8-5-1/2 and ex8-6-16, whose answers are non-integer or the ±5 window) so M lands on a whole-number lattice point within ±5, as pair_plotter requires. Row 3 (both endpoints negative in both coordinates) is the one built to surface the sign-dropping slip as wrong-quadrant. checks-only-one-coordinate is not diagnosable here: it describes comparing two already-computed midpoints (e.g. to confirm diagonals bisect each other), not placing one midpoint, so no anchor question in this LO's list actually exercises it.
